rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised victory belongs to whoever fears standing before God for reckoning and recompense; the possessive in ‘My station’ reflects that people stand by His command.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك الفوز لمن خاف وقوفه للحساب والجزاء بين يدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat they make to return the messengers to their religion reflects either a false belief that the messengers had once followed it or an assumption based on their origins.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا أو لتعودن في ملتنا وهم لم يكونوا على ملتهم قط إما لأنهم توهموا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The messengers asked God for victory over the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: طلبت الرسل الفتح والنصر من قبل الله تعالى على الكفار عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The messengers asked God for victory over the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: طلبت الرسل الفتح والنصر من قبل الله تعالى على الكفار عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: They asked God to judge between the messengers and their peoples; fatḥ can mean judgment and al-Fattāḥ a judge.
rows.anchor: هو سؤالهم أن يحكم الله بينهم وبين أممهم لأن الفتح الحكم والفتاح الحاكم عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the unbelievers mockingly asked for the punishment the prophets had threatened.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه واستفتح الكفار العذاب الذي توعدهم به الأنبياء على جهة التكذيب لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ‘stubborn tyrant’ is an arrogant opponent who turns away from and repels the truth.
rows.anchor: كل متكبر معاند مجانب للحق دافع له

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Hell is before the tyrant, waiting ahead of him along with his loss.
rows.anchor: جهنم بين يدي هذا الجبار عن الزجاج أي له مع الخيبة نار جهنم بين يديه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Hell is behind him; future time can be called ‘behind’ because it comes and overtakes a person from behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه من خلفه وإنما جاز في الزمان أن يسمى الأمام وراء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله ع
rows.claim: The drink is the blood and pus flowing from the private parts of adulterers in Hell; most commentators share this interpretation.
rows.anchor: من الدم والقيح من فروج الزواني في النار عن أبي عبد الله ع وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it looks like water but has the color and taste of pus.
rows.anchor: أو لونه لون الماء وطعمه طعم الصديد

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: The Prophet says that the drink scorches the face and makes the scalp fall when brought near, then cuts through the drinker’s intestines; the report links this punishment to 47:15 and 18:29.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A wine drinker’s prayer is not accepted for forty days; if he dies with wine inside him, God gives him the pus of Hell’s people, including the gathered emissions of adulterers, which melts his insides and skin.
rows.anchor: من شرب الخمر لم تقبل له صلاة أربعين يوما فإن مات وفي بطنه شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The source identifies the transmitters of the preceding wine-and-Hell report as Shuʿayb ibn Wāqid, al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd, al-Ṣādiq, and his forefathers.
rows.anchor: رواه شعيب بن واقد عن الحسين بن زيد عن الصادق ع عن آبائه ع عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned person drinks the pus in repeated sips and can scarcely swallow it: its heat and stench repel him, but he is forced to drink.
rows.anchor: أي يشرب ذلك الصديد جرعة جرعة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: Death’s agonies reach every part of the body, inside and out, even the tips of the hair.
rows.anchor: شدائد الموت وسكراته من كل موضع من جسده ظاهره وباطنه حتى تأتيه من أطراف شعره عن إبراهيم التيمي وابن جريج

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Death’s agonies reach every part of the body, inside and out, even the tips of the hair.
rows.anchor: شدائد الموت وسكراته من كل موضع من جسده ظاهره وباطنه حتى تأتيه من أطراف شعره عن إبراهيم التيمي وابن جريج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alternatively, death confronts him from every direction and takes him from above, below, both sides, before, and behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل يحضره الموت من كل موضع ويأخذه من كل جانب من فوقه ومن تحته وعن يمينه وشماله ومن قدامه وخلفه عن ابن عباس والجبائي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Alternatively, death confronts him from every direction and takes him from above, below, both sides, before, and behind.
rows.anchor: ويأخذه من كل جانب من فوقه ومن تحته وعن يمينه وشماله ومن قدامه وخلفه عن ابن عباس والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite death’s causes and torments, he does not die and find relief, as in the verse about the people of Hell not being made to die.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح وهذا كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment behind him is eternal residence in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وهو الخلود في النار

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Alternatively, after the punishment already described comes a still more severe and painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه ومن بعد هذا العذاب الذي سبق ذكره عذاب أشد وأوجع مما تقدم عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The comparison means the works of those who disbelieve; the construct phrase omits ‘works’ before ‘those who disbelieve’ because it is repeated afterward.
rows.anchor: مثل أعمال الذين كفروا بربهم فحذف المضاف اعتمادا على ذكره بعد المضاف إليه عن الفراء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the likeness of the unbelievers themselves among what has been related about them.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه مما نقص عليك مثل الذين كفروا عن سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds yield little benefit: like ashes scattered by a violent wind, they cannot be gathered or used; this parallels the verse about works made scattered dust.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقدرون على الانتفاع بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The far misguidance is the deeds’ remoteness from benefit.
rows.anchor: يعني أن عملهم ذلك هو الذهاب البعيد عن النفع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is error far removed from what is right.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخطأ البعيد عن الصواب عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes determinism because it attributes the deeds to the unbelievers; if God created those deeds, attributing them to the people would be invalid.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة واضحة على بطلان قول المجبرة لأنه أضاف العمل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation variants for ‘mufraṭūn’ differ: Nāfiʿ and Qutayba from al-Kisāʾī have silent fāʾ, kasra on rāʾ, and no gemination; Abū Jaʿfar has fatḥa and geminated rāʾ; the remaining readers have silent fāʾ and fatḥa on rāʾ; al-Aʿraj is also reported with fatḥa and gemination.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وقتيبة عن الكسائي مفرطون ساكنة الفاء مكسورة الراء خفيفة وقرأ أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses one form as ‘left behind’; another explanation is ‘sent ahead’ because farṭ means going ahead, hence advanced to Hell.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج أما تفسير مفرطون فجاء عن ابن عباس متروكون وقيل معجلون ومعنى الفرط في اللغة التقدم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The ‘sent ahead’ reading means they are placed ahead in the Fire and left there forever in punishment.
rows.anchor: فمعنى مفرطون مقدمون إلى النار وكذلك مفرطون بالتشديد ومن فسر متروكون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The reading with fatḥa on rāʾ describes people who neglected the afterlife in worldly life, as confirmed by the verse about regret for neglecting God’s cause.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ مفرطون فالمعنى أنه وصفهم الله بأنهم فرطوا في الدنيا ولم يعملوا فيها للآخرة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another reading means they went to excess in disobeying God, choosing and advancing their failure.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ مفرطون فالمراد أنهم أفرطوا في معصية الله كما تقول أفرط فلان في مكروهي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The intensified form can mean that they possess precedence toward the Fire and were first to reach it, like other forms denoting possession of a quality.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي وكأنه من أفرط أي صار ذا فرط مثل أقطف وأجرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the syntax, ‘the lie’ is the object of ‘describe’; ‘that they have the best’ substitutes for ‘the lie’; the clause that they have the Fire is accusative with jarama, though Qutrub allows a nominative analysis.
rows.anchor: الكذب مفعول تصف وأن لهم الحسنى بدل من الكذب وتقديره وتصف ألسنتهم أن لهم

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub parses ‘that they have the Fire’ as nominative, meaning that it is established that they have the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن أن في موضع رفع عن قطرب قال معناه أنه وجب أن لهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God immediately punished all people for their wrongdoing, no creature on the earth who deserved punishment would remain; ‘on it’ refers implicitly to the earth.
rows.anchor: لو كان ممن يؤاخذ الكفار والعصاة بذنوبهم ويعاجلهم بالعقوبة لما ترك على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic commonly omits an understood place, as in ‘between its two lava fields’ for Medina and ‘it became cold’ for the morning.
rows.anchor: لأن الكلام يدل عليه فإن العلم حاصل بأن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is Judgment Day, or a time God knows it is no longer beneficial to keep them alive because they will not believe and no believer will descend from them; postponement nevertheless allows repentance or serves a benefit.
rows.anchor: أي يمهلهم إلى وقت معلوم مسمى وهو يوم القيامة وقيل إلى وقت يعلمه الله تعالى أنه لا يكون في بقائهم فيه مصلحة

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: On whether someone known never to believe may be spared, Abū Hāshim and al-Murtaḍā say continued life is permissible but not obligatory, since moral responsibility itself is a grace.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي هاشم وإليه ذهب المرتضى قدس الله روحه

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: On whether someone known never to believe may be spared, Abū Hāshim and al-Murtaḍā say continued life is permissible but not obligatory, since moral responsibility itself is a grace.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي هاشم وإليه ذهب المرتضى قدس الله روحه

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī and Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī require continued life, but differ: al-Jubbāʾī calls its absence harmful, while al-Balkhī calls preservation the most beneficial choice; al-Mufīd agrees with al-Balkhī.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون لا يجوز احترامه ويجب تبقيته وهو قول البلخي وأبي علي الجبائي وإن اختلفا في علته

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī and Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī require continued life, but differ: al-Jubbāʾī calls its absence harmful, while al-Balkhī calls preservation the most beneficial choice; al-Mufīd agrees with al-Balkhī.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي: لأنه مفسدة وقال البلخي لأنه الأصلح

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Alternatively, if God punished them, He would withhold rain until every animal perished.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن معنى الآية لو يؤاخذهم بذنوبهم لحبس المطر عنهم حتى تهلك كل دابة عن السدي وعكرمة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Alternatively, if God punished them, He would withhold rain until every animal perished.
rows.anchor: لحبس المطر عنهم حتى تهلك كل دابة عن السدي وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question asks why animals without guilt would suffer if wrongdoers deserve punishment. The answer is that their suffering is a lesson and trial, with compensation, like illness affecting saints and those not morally responsible.
rows.anchor: أن العذاب للظالم عقوبة ولغير الظالم عبرة ومحنة فيكون كالأمراض النازلة بالأولياء وغير المكلفين فيعوضون عنها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, if the fathers perished through disbelief, their children would never exist.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه لو هلك الآباء بكفرهم لم يوجد الأبناء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, animals were created for morally responsible people, so there would be no purpose in their continuing after those people perished.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه إذا هلك الظلمة ولم يبق مكلف لا يبقى غيرهم من الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that people cannot delay or advance their appointed time was explained earlier.
rows.anchor: قد سبق معناه فيما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists assign to God the daughters they themselves dislike.
rows.anchor: يعني البنات أي يحكمون لله بما يكرهونه لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The ‘best outcome’ their tongues claim is sons.
rows.anchor: البنون عن مجاهد وقيل معناه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, they claim that despite their ugly speech they will receive a good reward and Paradise; they said that if Muḥammad’s account of resurrection were true, they would be people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه تصفون أن لهم مع قبيح قولهم من الله الجزاء الحسن والمثوبة الحسنى وهي الجنة عن الزجاج وغيره

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muʿādh recited al-kadhb with ḍamma on dhāl and bāʾ, making it a plural adjective for lying tongues, ‘liars’ or ‘great liars.’
rows.anchor: وروي عن معاذ أنه قرأ وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب بضم الذال والباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘No doubt’ means that their deed and statement make it certain they will have the Fire; commentators gloss it as ‘truly’ or ‘inevitably.’
rows.anchor: أي ليس الأمر على ما وصفوا جرم فعلهم وقولهم أي كسب أن لهم النار والمفسرون يقولون معناه حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘mufraṭūn’ means they are sent ahead, hastened to the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي مقدمون أي معجلون إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among earlier peoples Satan made disbelief, error, and denial of messengers seem attractive.
rows.anchor: أي كفرهم وضلالهم وتكذيبهم الرسل

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Satan is their ally in worldly life, when they follow his seduction; on Judgment Day the followers disown one another.
rows.anchor: يتولونه ويتبعون إغوائه فأما يوم القيامة فيتبرأ بعضهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Satan is their ally on Judgment Day because God abandons them to him in despair of mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه فهو وليهم يوم القيامة أي يكلهم الله تعالى إلى الشيطان أياسا لهم من رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the follower and the one followed will suffer painful punishment.
rows.anchor: ولهم عذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was sent so Muḥammad could clarify disputes over monotheism, divine justice, and what is lawful and unlawful; it is guidance and mercy for believers.
rows.anchor: معناه إلا وقد أردنا منك أن تكشف لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain revives parched land with plants; this is a proof for people who listen by attending to God’s signs, reflecting, and taking heed.
rows.anchor: أحياها بالنبات بعد جدوبها وقحطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ‘We give you drink,’ Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, Yaʿqūb, and Sahl read with fatḥa on nūn; the rest use ḍamma, while Abū Jaʿfar reads with tāʾ in al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب وسهل نسقيكم بفتح النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbs may distinguish handing someone a drink (saqaytu) from providing water (asqaytu), or asking God to water someone; others treat them as synonyms or distinguish a single drink from ongoing provision.
rows.anchor: قيل بين سقيت وأسقيت فرق وهو أن سقيته معناه ناولته ليشرب وأسقيته معناه جعلت له ماء يشربه

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhū al-Rumma’s line uses asqaytu for providing or asking that someone be watered, with the speaker sharing his grief with stones and dwellings.
rows.anchor: وأسقيه حتى كاد مما أبثه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says saqaytu is for giving a drink once, while asqaytu can describe giving drink continually.
rows.anchor: إذا سقاه مرة يقول سقيته وإذا سقاه دائما يقال أسقيته عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s line uses both verb forms for the tribes, supporting their synonymous use.
rows.anchor: سقى قومي بني مجد وأسقى نميرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘lesson’ is an instructive sign; farth is material that descends into the stomach, and sāʾigh describes food that passes easily through the throat.
rows.anchor: الفرث الثفل الذي ينزل إلى الكرش وساغ الطعام في الحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukr has four senses: an intoxicating drink; food or taste, as in the poet’s line about making nobles’ faults a taste; stillness, as in a quiet night or wind; and the verbal noun of sakira, including confusion of sight.
rows.anchor: السكر في اللغة على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhulul is the plural of dhalul, while radhil and radhāl mean low or poor quality.
rows.anchor: الذلل جمع الذلول يقال دابة ذلول بين الذل ورجل ذلول

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘its bellies’ can agree with al-anʿām as a masculine collective; another explanation refers it to one animal, as in a poet’s wording that returns to milk.
rows.anchor: الهاء في بطونه إلى ماذا يعود اختلف فيه فقيل إن الأنعام جمع والجمع يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: الصلتان العبدي
rows.claim: Al-Ṣaltān al-ʿAbdī’s line shows agreement based on meaning: two feminine nouns are treated as a masculine dual subject.
rows.anchor: إن السماحة والمروءة ضمنا قبرا بمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the agreement discussion allows the pronoun to refer to the milk-bearing animals intended, and min may be partitive because only some livestock produce milk.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير نسقيكم مما في بطون المذكور وقيل إن من يدل على التبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘from it you make an intoxicant,’ the pronoun can refer to the fruits already mentioned or to thamarāt as a collective equivalent to thamar.
rows.anchor: الضمير في منه إلى ماذا يعود فيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The healing pronoun can refer to honey or the Qur’an; with honey, ‘healing’ is predicated through the prepositional phrase, while the Qur’an reading raises a different syntactic question.
rows.anchor: الهاء في قوله فيه شفاء للناس قيل يعود إلى الشراب وهو العسل وقيل يعود إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: For ‘so that after knowledge he knows nothing,’ Sibawayh makes ‘nothing’ the object of ʿalima and leaves the object of yaʿlamu implicit by way of explanation.
rows.anchor: إن نصبت شيئا بعلم وهو مذهب سيبويه كنت قد أعملت الثاني وأضمرت المفعول في يعلم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ instead makes yaʿlamu operative, omits an object for ʿalima, and separates the object from its governing verb, combining two figurative constructions.
rows.anchor: وإن أعملت يعلم وهو مذهب الفراء أضمرت لعلم مفعولا وفصلت بين المعمول والعامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock—camels, cattle, and sheep—are an instructive sign of God’s power and wondrous design.
rows.anchor: أي لعظة واعتبارا ودلالة على قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that fodder settles in the stomach: the lower part becomes dung, the upper blood, and the middle milk; blood enters the veins, milk the udder, and dung remains unmixed.
rows.anchor: وروى الكلبي عن ابن عباس قال إذا استقر العلف في الكرش صار أسفله فرثا وأعلاه دما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The milk is pure, without blood or dung, and pleasant to swallow; the liver distributes these substances according to divine design.
rows.anchor: أي جائزا في حلوقهم والكبد مسلطة على هذه الأصناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who deny resurrection, the one who can extract drinkable white milk from dung and blood can likewise bring the dead from earth without mixing their bodies with others.
rows.anchor: من قدر على إخراج لبن أبيض سائغ من بين الفرث والدم من غير أن يختلط بهما قادر على إخراج الموتى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One construction means that people have a lesson in what God produced from the fruits of palms and grapes.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه ولكم عبرة فيما أخرج الله لكم من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another construction supplies the omitted relative ‘what’: from the fruits of palms and grapes, you make what becomes an intoxicant; Arabs often omit the relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب ما تتخذون منه سكرا والعرب تضمر ما الموصولة كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further construction supplies an omitted noun: ‘something’ from the fruits of palms and grapes that you make into an intoxicant.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن تقديره ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب شيء تتخذون منه سكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intoxicant is wine or any intoxicating drink, while good provision is lawful products such as vinegar, raisins, syrup, fresh dates, and dried dates, according to several early authorities.
rows.anchor: والأعناب عطف على الثمرات أي ومن الأعناب شيء تتخذون سكرا وهو كل ما يسكر من الشراب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report preserved by al-Ḥākim, Ibn ʿAbbās says ‘intoxicant’ is what is forbidden from the fruits and ‘good provision’ what is lawful.
rows.anchor: وروى الحاكم في صحيحه بالإسناد عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن هذه الآية فقال السكر ما حرم من ثمرها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the verse was revealed before wine was prohibited and that its prohibition came later in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة نزلت الآية قبل تحريم الخمر ونزل تحريمها بعد ذلك في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says there is no need to place the verse before the prohibition: it addresses polytheists and counts their blessings, including wine as one of their drinks.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم ولا حاجة إلى ذلك سواء كان الخمر حراما أم لم يكن لأنه تعالى خاطب المشركين

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and al-Jubbāʾī interpret ‘intoxicant’ as permissible kinds of drink and ‘good provision’ as food, the pleasant things people eat.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المراد بالسكر ما يشرب من أنواع الأشربة مما يحل

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and al-Jubbāʾī interpret ‘intoxicant’ as permissible kinds of drink and ‘good provision’ as food, the pleasant things people eat.
rows.anchor: والرزق الحسن ما يؤكل والحسن اللذيذ عن الشعبي والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not authorize nabīdh: it reports what people did with the fruits, just as another verse reports making oaths a means of deception; describing a use does not license it.
rows.anchor: وقد أخطأ من تعلق بهذه الآية في تحليل النبيذ لأنه سبحانه إنما أخبر عن فعل كانوا يتعاطونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created these fruits for people’s benefit, but people also made forbidden things from them.
rows.anchor: أنه سبحانه أخبر أنه خلق هذه الثمار لينتفعوا بها فاتخذوا منها ما هو محرم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variety of useful fruit products is a sign for people who reason; God’s extraction of juice from mixed fruit points to His ability to recover the dispersed dead from soil.
rows.anchor: عن الله تعالى ذلك ويتفكرون فيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration, either according to al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid or as an instinct planted in it that other creatures do not perceive, also attributed to al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: أي ألهمها إلهاما عن الحسن وابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration, either according to al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid or as an instinct planted in it that other creatures do not perceive, also attributed to al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: أي ألهمها إلهاما عن الحسن وابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God’s revelation to the bee means inspiration, either according to al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid or as an instinct planted in it that other creatures do not perceive, also attributed to al-Ḥasan.
rows.anchor: أي ألهمها إلهاما عن الحسن وابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda lists Arabic senses of waḥy: prophetic revelation, inspiration, gesture, writing, and secret communication; he illustrates them with the cited Qur’anic passages.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الوحي في كلام العرب على وجوه منها وحي النبوة ومنها الإلهام ومنها الإشارة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains ‘he signaled to them’ as a gesture; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means he wrote for them.
rows.anchor: في قوله فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا قال مجاهد معناه أشار إليهم وقال الضحاك كتب لهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains ‘he signaled to them’ as a gesture; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means he wrote for them.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد معناه أشار إليهم وقال الضحاك كتب لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s statement that there is no revelation except the Qur’an refers to the Qur’an as the revelation brought by Gabriel to Muḥammad, not to every Arabic sense of waḥy.
rows.anchor: وأما ما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال لا وحي إلا القرآن فإن المراد به أن القرآن هو الوحي الذي نزل به جبرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, waḥy is discreet, concealed communication; both awḥā lahu and awḥā ilayhi are used.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوحي عند العرب أن يلقي الإنسان إلى صاحبه شيئا بالاستتار والإخفاء

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line about the ground being told to settle illustrates waḥy as concealed communication or inspiration.
rows.anchor:
قال العجاج:
أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired the bee to make homes for honey in mountains, trees, and other places, a capacity no person could devise without divine instruction.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن الله تعالى ألهم النحل اتخاذ المنازل والمساكن والأوكار والبيوت في الجبال والشجر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: ‘From what people build’ can refer to grape arbors or to the beehives people construct; yaʿrishūn has two vowel patterns and can mean they build, from ʿarsh as a roof.
rows.anchor: والعرش سقف البيت عن الكلبي والمعنى ما يبني الناس لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bee receives commands in the wording because the verse first describes what is inspired to it, a rhetorical extension despite its inability to understand speech.
rows.anchor: وإنما أتى بلفظ الأمر وإن كانت النحل لا تعقل الأمر ولا تكون مأمورة لأنه لما أتى بلفظ الوحي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The bee’s ‘tamed’ paths are made smooth, open, and wide for travel.
rows.anchor: صفة للسبل وهي منصوبة على الحال وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘tamed’ describes the bees as obedient, submissive, and made subject to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل ذللا أي مطيعة لله منقادة مسخرة ويكون من صفة النحل عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey varies in color—white, yellow, or reddish—because bees take from different plants and flowers; although it comes from the belly, they release it from the mouth like saliva.
rows.anchor: وهو العسل فإن ألوانه مختلفة لأن منه ما هو شديد البياض ومنه ما هو أصفر ومنه ما يضرب إلى الحمرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Honey heals illnesses, according to Qatāda; al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan specify diseases for which honey is an effective remedy.
rows.anchor: من الأدواء عن قتادة وروي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Honey heals illnesses, according to Qatāda; al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan specify diseases for which honey is an effective remedy.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه فيه شفاء للأوجاع التي شفاؤها فيه عن السدي والحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Honey heals illnesses, according to Qatāda; al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan specify diseases for which honey is an effective remedy.
rows.anchor: فيه شفاء للأوجاع التي شفاؤها فيه عن السدي والحسن

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says to use the two cures: the Qur’an and honey.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال عليكم بالشفاءين القرآن والعسل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid takes the pronoun in ‘in it is healing’ to refer to the Qur’an, whose law, prohibitions, legal opinions, and rulings heal people.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أن الهاء في فيه راجعة إلى القرآن أي القرآن فيه شفاء للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators take the pronoun to mean honey, and this is stronger because the Qur’an had not been mentioned before the pronoun.
rows.anchor: والأول قول أكثر المفسرين وهو الأقوى إذا لم يسبق للقرآن ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bee offers several signs: honey comes from its mouth, healing comes from the source of its sting, and its construction and nature contain wonders.
rows.anchor: وفي النحل والعسل وجوه من الاعتبار منها اختصاصه بخروج العسل من فيه ومنها جعل الشفاء من موضع السم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each bee group has a leader that protects, directs, and governs it; the followers track it, and the group’s order collapses if it is lost.
rows.anchor: ومن أعجبها أن جعل سبحانه لك فئة يعسوبا

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين ع
rows.claim: The author connects the bee’s leader to ʿAlī’s saying, ‘I am the leader of the believers.’
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا المعنى فيما قال أشار أمير المؤمنين ع في قوله أنا يعسوب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created people, bestowed worldly and religious blessings, and then takes their lives.
rows.anchor: أي أوجدكم وأنعم عليكم بضروب النعم الدينية والدنيوية

rows.speaker: علي ع
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī gives seventy-five years as the age of extreme old age; a similar report is attributed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن علي ع أن أرذل العمر خمس وسبعون سنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī gives seventy-five years as the age of extreme old age; a similar report is attributed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: خمس وسبعون سنة وروي في مثل ذلك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda puts the age of extreme old age at ninety years.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة تسعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At extreme old age people return toward childhood, forgetting what they once knew; alternatively, their knowledge simply diminishes compared with youth.
rows.anchor: أي ليرجع إلى حال الطفولة بنسيان ما كان علمه لأجل الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what benefits His servants and has power over whatever He wills in managing and determining their circumstances.
rows.anchor: على ما يشاء من تدبيرهم وتقدير أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hand tied to the neck portrays refusing to give; spreading it fully portrays giving away everything and becoming wasteful.
rows.anchor: أي لا تكن ممن لا يعطي شيئا ولا يهب فتكون بمنزلة من يده مغلولة إلى عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of a fully spread hand is a metaphor for extravagance; ‘blamed’ means one blames oneself and others blame one.
rows.anchor: أي ولا تعط أيضا جميع ما عندك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: ‘Exhausted’ means left with nothing and no means.
rows.anchor: منقطعا به وليس عندك شيء عن السدي وابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ‘Exhausted’ means left with nothing and no means.
rows.anchor: منقطعا به وليس عندك شيء عن السدي وابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means incapable and regretful.
rows.anchor: وقيل عاجزا نادما عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله ع
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means stripped of clothing and naked.
rows.anchor: وقيل محسورا من الثياب والمحسور العريان عن أبي عبد الله ع

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains the outcomes together: if stingy, one sits blamed; if extravagant, one remains distressed and regretful.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه إن أمسكت قعدت ملوما مذموما وإن أسرفت بقيت متحسرا مغموما عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says that giving everything leaves nothing for later requesters, who then blame the giver.
rows.anchor: لا تعط ما عندك جميعا فيجيء الآخرون يسألونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a woman sent her son to ask the Prophet for a garment; when told to ask for his shirt, he gave it, leaving himself unable to dress for prayer and prompting unbelievers to mock his absence.
rows.anchor: وروي أن امرأة بعثت ابنها إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kahf is a spacious cave in a mountain; a smaller cave is called a ghār.
rows.anchor: الكهف المغارة في الجبل إلا أنه واسع فإذا صغر فهو غار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raqīm derives from writing and means a written record; the word also names a mark on cloth and a patterned snake, while raqmat al-wādī is the water-bearing channel.
rows.anchor: والرقيم أصله من الرقم وهو الكتابة يقال رقمت الكتاب أرقمه فهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awā means to return or take refuge; futiya is a collective plural for young men, like ṣabī/ṣibya and ghulām/ghilma, though such formations are not fully productive.
rows.anchor: والأوي الرجوع والفتية جمع فتى وفعلة من أسماء الجمع وليس بناء يقاس عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We struck their ears’ means that God imposed sleep on them; the phrase is eloquent, like saying an emir struck someone’s hand to prevent action.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ضربنا على آذانهم سلطنا عليهم النوم وهو من الكلام البالغ في الفصاحة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub compares the expression to the Arabic idiom ‘the emir struck his hand,’ meaning he prevented him from acting.
rows.anchor: قال قطرب هو كقول العرب ضرب الأمير على يد فلان إذا منعه من التصرف

rows.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
rows.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur’s line ‘the earth was struck against me with barriers’ illustrates the idiom of being blocked or confined.
rows.anchor:
قال الأسود بن يعفر وكان ضريرا:
ومن الحوادث لا أبا لك أنني
ضربت علي الأرض بالأسداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A party is a group and amad is an endpoint; al-Nābigha’s racing line uses amad for the finish or limit.
rows.anchor:
قال النابغة:
إلا لمثلك أو من أنت سابقه
سبق الجواد إذا استولى على الأمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Years, counted’ is either an adverbial time expression with counted as a verbal noun or an adjective meaning years that are counted; Zajjāj says the extra count emphasizes that they were many.
rows.anchor: سنين نصب على الظرف وعددا منصوب على ضربين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects parsing amadan as a specification (tamyīz): if a past verb is intended, the word is its object, meaning which party counted a period of their stay.
rows.anchor:
قال أبو علي:
إن انتصابه على التمييز عندي غير مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a past verb is intended, amadan is the object of aḥṣā: the question is which party counted a period for their stay.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان ماضيا كان المعنى لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى أمدا للبثهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq transmits from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that Quraysh sent al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ to Jewish scholars in Medina to ask about three signs: ancient youths, a world traveler, and the spirit.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة عن ابن عباس أن النضر بن الحرث بن كلدة وعقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: أحبار اليهود
rows.claim: The Jewish scholars told the envoys to ask about the youths, the traveler who reached the East and West, and the spirit; if Muḥammad answered the first two but not the last, he was still a prophet.
rows.anchor: فقال لهما أحبار اليهود اسألوه عن ثلاث فإن أخبركم بهن فهو نبي مرسل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked, the Prophet said he would answer the next day but did not say ‘if God wills’; revelation then ceased for fifteen nights, and Meccans spread rumors while the delay distressed him.
rows.anchor: فجاؤوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسألوه فقال:

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the cave chapter then came through Gabriel with answers about the youths and traveler, along with the revelation about the spirit.
rows.anchor: ثم جاءه جبرائيل ع عن الله سبحانه بسورة الكهف وفيها ما سألوه عنه عن أمر الفتية والرجل الطواف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths took refuge in the cave to escape their people and protect their religion, asking God for mercy, rescue, and a way to right guidance.
rows.anchor: أي اذكر لقومك إذا التجأ أولئك الشبان إلى الكهف وجعلوه مأواهم هربا بدينهم إلى الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The prayer may ask God to provide a safe way out of the cave.
rows.anchor: وقيل هيىء لنا مخرجا من الغار في سلامة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they ask to be guided to a course that will save them, or for an arrangement that earns God’s approval.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه دلنا على أمر فيه نجاتنا لأن الرشد والنجاة بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths were believers who concealed Islam from a ruler named Daqiyānūs in Ephesus; he worshiped idols and killed opponents, though another account calls him a Magian who promoted that religion.
rows.anchor: وكان اسم الملك دقيانوس واسم مدينتهم أفسوس وكان ملكهم يعبد الأصنام ويدعو إليها

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the youths were close associates of the king who hid their faith from one another until they met, disclosed it, and fled to the cave.
rows.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير وقيل إنهم كانوا قبل بعث عيسى ع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says they followed the religion of Jesus after the people of the Gospel had passed away; another places them before Jesus’s mission.
rows.anchor: على دين المسيح لما برح أهل الإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them sleep for many counted years, answering their prayer and blocking sound from reaching them; this shows they remained alive and slept safely and peacefully.
rows.anchor: معناه أنمناهم سنين ذات عدد وتأويله فأجبنا دعاءهم وسددنا آذانهم بالنوم الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is among the Qur’an’s eloquent idioms and cannot be translated while preserving its wording’s full force.
rows.anchor: وهذا من فصيح لغات القرآن التي لا يمكن أن يترجم بمعنى يوافق اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God woke them so the two groups could determine how long they had stayed; the event makes God’s previously known matter manifest, rather than adding knowledge to Him.
rows.anchor: أي ليظهر معلومنا على ما علمناه وذكرنا الوجه في أمثاله فيما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups may be believers and unbelievers among the people of the cave, or the youths themselves after waking, since they disputed how long they had slept; the dispute is reflected in 18:19.
rows.anchor: وقيل يعني بالحزبين أصحاب الكهف لما استيقظوا اختلفوا في تعداد لبثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave story follows the account of the earth’s adornment and trial because the youths abandoned worldly beauty, chose obedience, and left home and property, inviting imitation.
rows.anchor: أنه لما أخبر عن زينة الأرض وعن الابتلاء عقبه بذكر الفتية التي تركت زينة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave story also follows the Prophet’s grief over unbelievers: he should not despair, since God will support and protect him as He protected the youths.
rows.anchor: أنه اتصل بقوله: { فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم } أي فلا تأسف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third link is the promise to give believers good news: God will support them as He supported the people of the cave.
rows.anchor: أنه اتصل بقوله: { ويبشر المؤمنين } أي وينصرهم كما نصر أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For marfiqan, people of Medina, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Aʿshā, and al-Barjamī from Abū Bakr read fatḥa on mīm and kasra on fāʾ; the other readers reverse those vowels.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر والأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر مرفقا بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and Quṭrub acknowledge both vowel forms for ‘benefit/support’ and ‘joint’; kasra on the arm-joint form is more idiomatic.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وذكر قطرب وغيره اللغتين جميعا في مرفق الأمر ومرفق اليد

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says the fatḥa form means a thing used for benefit, while the kasra form is a noun; it may be a dialect or a verbal noun form.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن مرفقا أي شيئا يرتفقون به مثل المقطع ونحوه ومرفقا جعله اسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shataṭ means exceeding a boundary through excess; the root evokes remoteness, and the same root can describe excessive height or overpricing.
rows.anchor: الشطط الخروج عن الحد بالغلو فيه وأصله مجاوزة الحد في البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtizāl means withdrawing or distancing oneself; a line of poetry uses taʿazzul for withdrawal, and the name Muʿtazila was applied to ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd’s circle because they left al-Ḥasan’s gathering.
rows.anchor: والاعتزال التنحي عن الأمر والتعزل بمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra in innahum fitya begins a new sentence; idh qāmū is attached to ‘We strengthened,’ and shataṭan is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: إذ قاموا يتعلق بربطنا أي في الوقت الذي قاموا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls them youths because they believed and increased in insight and desire to remain firm through gracious assistance that strengthened their commitment.
rows.anchor: أي بصيرة في الدين ورغبة في الثبات عليه بالألطاف المقوية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid defines futuwwa as generosity, refraining from harm, and not complaining.
rows.anchor: الفتوة بذل الندى وترك الأذى وترك الشكوى عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another definition of futuwwa is avoiding forbidden things and practicing noble conduct.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي اجتناب المحارم واستعمال المكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened their hearts with faith-firming graces and thoughts so they could proclaim truth, endure hardship, and leave home.
rows.anchor: أي شددنا عليها بالألطاف والخواطر المقوية للإيمان حتى وطنوا أنفسهم على إظهار الحق والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spoke before Daqiyānūs, the tyrant who tested believers, declaring that their Lord created the heavens and earth and that calling on another god would be an extreme falsehood.
rows.anchor: حين قاموا بين يدي ملكهم الجبار دقيانوس الذي كان يفتن أهل الإيمان عن دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their people worship idols besides God but offer no clear proof; this condemns blind imitation and indicates that religion should be accepted only on clear evidence.
rows.anchor: أي هلا يأتون على عبادتهم غير الله بحجة ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is more unjust than a person who falsely claims that God has a partner in worship.
rows.anchor: فزعم أن له شريكا في العبادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Tamlikhā, the youths’ leader, spoke: if they left their people and idols, they would still not abandon worship of God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وهذا من قول تمليخا وهو رئيس أصحاب الكهف قال لهم فإذا فارقتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If some youths worshiped God alongside the idols, the exception ‘except God’ is connected; if all worshiped only idols, it is a disconnected exception.
rows.anchor: الاستثناء متصلا ويجوز أن يكون جميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should make the cave their refuge; God will spread mercy and arrange ease, gentleness, and what they need for their livelihood.
rows.anchor: أي صيروا إليه واجعلوه مأواكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the arrangement as God making their fear of the ruler and his injustice easy to bear, with gentleness and relief.
rows.anchor: ويسهل عليكم ما تخافون من الملك وظلمه ويأتيكم باليسر والرفق واللطف عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shows the high status of migration for religion and the wrongness of staying in an unbelieving land when remaining requires professing disbelief.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على عظم منزلة الهجرة في الدين وعلى قبح المقام في دار الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read tazāwar with gemination; the Kūfans lighten it; the other readers geminate it. Al-Ḥijāzīs geminate lummilt, while the others lighten it; al-Jaḥdarī has tazwār and al-Ḥasan reads the turning as an active verb.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ويعقوب تزور بتشديد الزاي وقرأ أهل الكوفة تزاور بالتخفيف والباقون تزاور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazāwar can derive from tatazāwar with assimilation of tāʾ into zāy, or from deletion of the second tāʾ; Abū al-Ḥasan objects that the form tazūr does not fit here, while Abū ʿAlī adduces Jarīr’s poetic use of azwirār for tents.
rows.anchor: من قرأ تزاور فإنه تتزاور فأدغم التاء في الزاي ومن قرأ تزاور حذف الثانية

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says tazūr has no suitable sense here and cites azwara ʿannī for withdrawing, as in ʿAntara’s poem about a spear wound.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: لا معنى له في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr’s verse describing tents with azwirār supports the use of a form meaning to turn or slant away.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي والذي حسن القراءة به قول جرير

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan considers the lighter lummilt more idiomatic, since people usually say ‘you filled me with fear’ rather than ‘fear filled me.’
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الخفيفة أجود لا يكادون يقولون ملأ مني رعبا وإنما يقولون ملأتني رعبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry by Imruʾ al-Qays and al-Aʿshā supports the lighter form, while al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī supplies an example of the intensified form.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي يدل على قول أبي الحسن قول امرىء القيس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s variant reads ‘and their turning’ as an active verb, with an understood verb such as ‘you see’ governing it.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الحسن وتقلبهم بفتح التاء والقاف والباء وضم اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarḍ can mean cutting across or passing by; al-Kisāʾī also gives it the sense of reciprocal recompense, as in Dhū al-Rumma’s line about traversing a valley.
rows.anchor: القرض القطع يقال قرضت الموضع إذا قطعته

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ uses qāraḍtuhum for trading insults: if you criticize them, they will criticize you.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء: إن قارضتهم قارضوك وإن تركتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other senses of qarḍ include a tooth’s gnawing, commercial partnership in Ḥijāz, and qaṣīda poetry, especially a poem distinct from rajaz.
rows.anchor: والقراض بلغة الحجاز المضاربة والقرض هو قول الشعر القصيدة منه خاصة دون الرجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajwa is an open space or courtyard; ayqāẓ is the plural of awake, ruqūd the plural of sleeping, and waṣīd is the entrance or closed door, with variant forms waṣīd/asīd and awṣada/aṣada.
rows.anchor: والفجوة المتسع من الأرض وجمعه فجوات وفجاء ممدود وفجوة الدار ساحتها والإيقاظ جمع يقظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses about sunrise, sunset, and the youths in the cave all depend on ‘you see’; their being in a spacious place is a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: كلاهما بجوابهما في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle bāsiṭ governs ‘his forelegs’ despite referring to the past, because the narrative depicts the scene as present.
rows.anchor: وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه أعمل اسم الفاعل حيث نصب به ذراعيه وإن كان بمعنى الماضي لأنه حكاية حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muṣḥaf writes al-muhtad here without yāʾ but writes it with yāʾ in al-Aʿrāf; deleting yāʾ is permitted in nouns but not verbs, where it marks jussive mood.
rows.anchor: كتب في المصحف هنا بغير ياء وفي الأعراف بالياء وحذف الياء جائز في الأسماء خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in iṭṭalaʿtum may have kasra, which is preferred between two vowelless consonants, or ḍamma by assimilation to wāw; ḍamma is favored when the next syllable is also ḍamma.
rows.anchor: لو اطلعت بكسر الواو ويجوز الضم والكسر أجود لأن الواو ساكنة والطاء ساكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firāran is a verbal noun because wallayta means ‘you fled’; raʿban is a specification, as in ‘filled with fear’ or ‘the vessel filled with water.’
rows.anchor: فرارا منصوب على المصدر لأن معنى وليت فررت ورعبا منصوب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sunrise the sun slants away to the right, and at sunset it passes to the left without entering the cave; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses taqriḍuhum as passing them at an angle.
rows.anchor: أي تميل وقت طلوعها عن كهفهم إلى جهة اليمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains taqriḍuhum as the sun passing them while turned away from them.
rows.anchor: تجاوزهم منحرفة عنهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the youths were in a broad open area inside the cave; the recess let in air but could not be seen from the entrance.
rows.anchor: في فضاء منه عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose a spacious, north-facing place that let in breezes while protecting the youths from sun, heat, fading skin color, and worn clothing; the cave mouth faced the Pole Star.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر سبحانه عن لطفه بهم وحفظه إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance made the youths rightly guided; the people of their community represent those left without a guiding protector.
rows.anchor: فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and others say the youths appeared awake because their eyes were open and they breathed as though about to speak, though they did not.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي وجماعة لأنهم مفتحو العيون يتنفسون كأنهم يريدون أن يتكلموا ولا يتكلمون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they turned over just as awake people do.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم ينقلبون كما ينقلب اليقظان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned them periodically from one side to the other so the earth would not consume them and their clothes would not decay from lying on one side.
rows.anchor: ونقلبهم تارة عن اليمين إلى الشمال وتارة عن الشمال إلى اليمين كما يتقلب النائم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that they were turned twice each year.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يقلبون كل عام تقلبتين عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that they were turned once each year.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان تقلبهم كل عام مرة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators say the youths fled their ruler by night, met a shepherd with a dog, and the dog followed them in their faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين أنهم هربوا من ملكهم ليلا فمروا براع معه كلب فتبعهم

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb gives another account: after repeatedly driving the dog away, the youths heard it say it loved God’s friends and would guard them, then it slept beside them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم مروا بكلب فتبعهم فطردوه فعاد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the dog was yellow.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان ذلك الكلب أصفر اللون عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the dog was spotted and named Qiṭmīr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان أنمر واسمه قطمير عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s commentary says the dog remained there for 309 years without food, drink, sleep, or rising.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الحسن أن ذلك الكلب مكث هناك ثلاثة مائة وتسع سنين بغير طعام ولا شراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāsiṭ dhirāʿayh means laying both forelegs flat on the ground, like a lion lying down.
rows.anchor: هو أن يلقيهما على الأرض مبسوطتين كافتراش السبع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Waṣīd means the cave’s courtyard according to Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Qatāda; others say the entrance, the recess entrance, or the threshold.
rows.anchor: أي بفنا الكهف عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī places the dog by the entrance of the recess, not the cave entrance, reasoning that searchers would otherwise have entered or found it; shepherds later moved the stones and used the opening as a livestock enclosure.
rows.anchor: وقيل بباب الفجوة أو فناء الفجوة لا باب الكهف لأن الكفار خرجوا إلى باب الكهف في طلبهم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says waṣīd is the door’s threshold.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الوصيد عتبة الباب عن عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who looked into the cave would flee in terror; God kept people away until the appointed time and protected the sleepers from predators and other harm.
rows.anchor: لو أشرفت عليهم ورأيتهم في كهفهم على حالتهم لفررت عنهم وأعرضت عنهم هربا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the eerie setting terrified people who came to the cave, and unbelievers sealed its entrance to kill the youths; God made this a protection for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا في مكان موحش من رآه فزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that long nails and hair caused the terror is unsound, since the youths later said they had slept only a day or part of one.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يصح لقوله تعالى حكاية عنهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports Ibn ʿAbbās telling Muʿāwiya during a Roman campaign that no one, even someone better than him, was permitted to uncover the youths; when Muʿāwiya sent men into the cave, God sent wind that drove them out.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال غزوت مع معاوية نحو الروم فمروا بالكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr, Ḥamza, and Khalaf read warq with a silent rāʾ, while the others use kasra; Abū ʿAmr and Abū Rajāʾ are reported with k-q assimilation, though Ibn Jinnī calls it concealment rather than true assimilation.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر وحمزة وخلف بورقكم ساكنة الراء والباقون بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī says the k-q sequence is concealed rather than assimilated; true assimilation would transfer the qāf’s kasra to rāʾ, and readers sometimes call concealment assimilation for convenience.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني هذا عند أصحابنا مخفي غير مدغم لكنه أخفى كسرة القاف فظنها القراء مدغمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘How long did you stay?’ means ‘how many days did you stay?’ with the counted unit omitted; kam is accusative as the object of labithtum.
rows.anchor: كم لبثتم تقديره كم يوما لبثتم فكم منصوبة بلبثتم والمميز محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘which food is purer/better’ is the object of ‘let him look,’ and ṭaʿāman is a specification.
rows.anchor: فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما الجملة التي هي أيها أزكى مفعول فلينظر وطعاما تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God woke them as He had preserved them for so long, producing an event that resembled resurrection.
rows.anchor: وكما فعلنا بهم الأمور العجيبة وحفظناهم تلك المدة المديدة بعثناهم من تلك الرقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their discussion of how long they had slept prompts recognition of their Creator and strengthens their certainty.
rows.anchor: ليكون بينهم تساؤل وتنازع واختلاف في مدة لبثهم فينتبهوا بذلك على معرفة صانعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators say they entered the cave in the morning and awoke near sunset, so they first guessed a day and then said perhaps part of a day when they saw the sun.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون إنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة وبعثهم الله في آخر النهار فلذلك قالوا يوما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Tamlikhā, their leader, was the one who returned the matter to God by saying their Lord knew how long they had remained.
rows.anchor: وهذا القائل هو تمليخا رئيسهم عن ابن عباس رد علم ذلك إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The silver coin was a dirham bearing the image of the ruler of their time; the city was the one they had left.
rows.anchor: والورق الدراهم وكان معهم دراهم عليها صورة الملك الذي كان في زمانهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the best food as the cleanest and lawfully slaughtered because most city residents were Magians, though some believers hid their faith.
rows.anchor: أي أطهر وأحل ذبيحة عن ابن عباس قال لأن عامتهم كانت مجوسا وفيهم قوم مؤمنون

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets azkā as tastier food.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أطيب طعاما عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima takes azkā as more plentiful, from the idea that wealth grows; the best food would be found where there was more of it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أكثر طعاما من قولهم زكى المال إذا زاد عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the city sold food that the youths considered impermissible.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان من طعام أهل المدينة ما لا يستحله أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoy should bring back some food and act discreetly; alternatively, he should shop gently without haggling or arguing with the seller.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وليتلطف في الشراء فلا يماكس البائع ولا ينازعه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: If the townspeople discover them, they may stone them to death, one of the worst killings.
rows.anchor: أي يقتلوكم بالرجم وهو من أخبث القتل عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘stone you’ means abuse or insult you verbally.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يؤذوكم ويشتموكم يقال رجمه بلسانه عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being restored to the townspeople’s religion means being invited back, not forced; alternatively, dissimulation may not have been permitted in that time.
rows.anchor: فالجواب يجوز أن يكون أراد يعيدوكم إلى دينهم بالاستدعاء دون الإكراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAthara means to come upon something; aʿthara means to reveal it, and an ʿāthūr is a pit dug to catch a lion, hence a person caught in trouble is said to have fallen into one.
rows.anchor: عثر على الشيء يعثر عثرا إذا طلع عليه وأعثرت عليه غيري والعاثور حفرة تحفر ليصطاد به الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marāʾ means disputation or argument.
rows.anchor: والمراء الجدال ماريت الرجل أماريه مراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase idh yatanaazaʿūn may attach to ‘We revealed them’ or to ‘so they would know.’
rows.anchor: إذ يتنازعون يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بقوله أعثرنا أي أطلعنا عليهم في وقت المنازعة

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says the first two number clauses describe the preceding indefinite number, while ‘and their eighth was their dog’ coordinates a sentence with another sentence; seven is a base number of emphasis.
rows.anchor: لأن ها هنا عطف جملة على جملة وهناك وصف النكرة بجملة فإن التقدير هم سبعة وهم ثلاثة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: An explanatory clause can follow what it explains without a conjunction.
rows.anchor: وأما الثالث: وهي الجملة التي تكون تفسيرا لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clause linked by a shared referent may connect to what precedes either with or without a conjunction.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا الوجه يتصل بما قبله على وجهين أحدهما: بحرف عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘believe in God’ clause following the invitation to a trade explains that trade; its imperative sense is phrased as a statement because an explanatory clause naturally takes declarative form, as the following ‘He will forgive you’ confirms.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تؤمنون بالله فتؤمنون على لفظ الخبر ومعناه الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example ‘they were beneficent before this’ followed without wāw by ‘they used to sleep little at night’ illustrates clauses linked by a shared referent; another verse uses wāw in a similar construction.
rows.anchor: ويقول في آية أخرى وكانوا يصرون بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘And their eighth was their dog’ is not a circumstantial clause, description, explanation, or wholly separate statement: the reported number is disputed, and the added wāw marks a link that shared reference alone does not supply.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون تفسيرا لأن التفسير هو المفسر في المعنى ولا يجوز أن يكون شيء من جزء الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause cannot modify the past participle as an adjective: a past participle does not operate as a present verb, and the sentence is independent rather than a descriptive clause.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز الأول لأنه في معنى الماضي والماضي لا يقدر فيه الانفصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw can be omitted from ‘their eighth is their dog’ because the clause itself mentions the people named before and thereby already signals the connection.
rows.anchor: فحذفت الواو واستغني عنها إذا كانت إنما تذكر لتدل على الاتصال وما في الجملة من ذكر ما في الأولى
